utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: We got a general task, and that was the task with which we went to Teslic between the 27th and the 28th of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Teslic, what did you find or who did you find in the police station and the jails within the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: First of all, when we arrived in Teslic on the morning of the 29th of June, we organised the army. There were about 700 soldiers. And first we took the police station with the soldiers. Then the hotel where the paramilitaries were accommodated, we disarmed them. There were two casualties. One person was killed among the paramilitaries and one on our side, among the policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you and let's break this down because you said one of the first things you did was we took the police station with the soldiers. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: We entered the police station which was under the control of the paramilitaries. There we disarmed the members of the paramilitary unit and called on all policemen to gather in the public security station for a meeting in order to discuss their further work and operations. Some of the soldiers went off in the direction of the hotel where most of the Mice were accommodated. And there, they disarmed them and arrested them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get there in just a minute. When you were within the police station, were there people in custody within the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were about 60 of them, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were those people that were in custody in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I think most of them were non-Serbs. I didn't see this myself, but I was told about it. One was a Jew, and there were a few Serbs, one or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were those the only 60 people being held in custody in the Teslic Municipality, or were there other people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. This was just one location. There were two other locations where there were non-Serbs. This was the playing field in Banja Teslic, and the building of the Territorial Defence staff. There was a building with several services in it, but I wasn't there myself because my task had only to do with the police station and the organisation of the policemen. But I know that all these centres were dissolved, and the people were allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when we talk about the people, what ethnicity are we talking about in these facilities that you've just described? Are they Serbian or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, they were Croats and Muslims. There were also others. I wasn't that familiar with Teslic, and it was Predrag Radulovic who dealt with those details because he was a local man, a native of Teslic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And why were these -- the non-Serbs in the police station and these facilities that you just described, why were they released?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the conviction of the team. People were not to blame for belonging to another ethnic group. And this was also the order of Stojan Zupljanin, the then chief of security service centre. First we had to see whether there were criminals among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the release of this -- and how many non-Serbs do you believe were released when you and the other officers arrived in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I think there were about 1.350 people in those three locations. I don't have the exact figure, but it has been recorded. I think there were over a thousand people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was done under the directive of the chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Correct. He issued us with those orders. But even had he not done so, we would have done that on our own. But he said: "Arrest them and disband or dissolve these collection centres."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about the last area, and that is the actual disarming and capture of the Mice. You told us earlier that the army was involved in it, and there might have been 700, 750 troops. Was this a procedure where you worked in conjunction with the army?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: We tried to reach an agreement with the army. It was mostly Predrag Radulovic who was in charge of that, but I do have this information. And one battalion of the Army of Republika Srpska was put at Predrag Radulovic's disposal. Predrag Radulovic also known as Pile. And on the night in question, we developed a plan as to how we should carry this out. And in the morning, at 5.00 a.m., in a factory compound, we began the operation, as we say in the police. And that's how we started implementing our plan. And unfortunately, this had tragic consequences because two people were killed. After they were disarmed and taken to a temporary prison, that was all we were able to do, help arrived from Banja Luka. Inspectors, professionals. And the police station in Teslic began operating normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back and talk about the members of the Mice that were taken into custody. First of all, did you manage to take each and every member of the Mice into custody?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: We took 21 men. That was the bulk of that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were they detained in custody?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Four or five were released during the investigation because we realised that they were only members of the group and that they did not commit any crimes. We filed criminal reports against 16 people charging them of various -- with various crimes. This is a very long criminal report which was sent to the competent prosecutor's office. After having completed our investigation in Teslic, we transported them in a vehicle to a prison in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why were they transferred to Banja Luka rather than being detained in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: This was in keeping with the law which we tried to apply to the maximum extent despite the war. In Teslic, we did not have conditions in place. That was one reason. And the second reason was their safety. For security reasons, we transported them to the prison which was in Banja Luka and which was in keeping with the law. And the third reason was that we had completed all the investigative procedure that had to do with the crimes that they had committed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In spite of the long list of crimes that the Mice committed, they were released. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out that they had been released?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: It just so happened because one of the 16 whose name I can't remember was found in a coffee bar in the evening when we were just patrolling the town. One of the inspectors called me and told me: "Boss, do you know that Mice had been released?" At first we couldn't believe that, and then we started fearing for our safety, and we increased our combat readiness to the highest level. We were afraid. We thought something bad would happen, but nothing bad happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you call Stojan Zupljanin to try to get an explanation as to what had happened? Did you ever talk to him about this, the release?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I didn't do it myself. There was a -- Predrag Radulovic, who was the head of the police, Predrag was very unhappy. He called Stojan and in an informal conversation, we had learned that Mice had been released. When we talked to Stojan, he himself was not aware of the fact that Mice had been released. It was Predrag who first told him when he called him from the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discover what Stojan's reaction was when he heard that the Mice had been released?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I never found out about his reaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever find out who was responsible for the ordering the release of the Mice?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I never found out, but I assume and I'm still convinced that it was somebody at the very top level of the government. Stojan himself could not have done that. I believe it was somebody much above him, somebody with a lot more influence and responsibility. Somebody at a very high level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that Mr. Brdjanin is at the top. But do you think that Mr. Brdjanin could have ordered the release of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I don't know Brdjanin personally, although I'm witnessing -- testifying here today. I know him from TV and from the media, but I believe that he could not have had much of a say there. I don't know whether he was even consulted on that matter. But in any case, I think it must have been somebody at a higher level. It could not have been even at Brdjanin's request because those people were from the area of Doboj. So if anybody had requested or asked for that, it could only have been somebody from that region, the region of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Can I have just a minute, Your Honours. Your Honour, that's all I have with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Cunningham, for that exemplary direct. Madam Chana, do you propose to start your cross-examination now, or do you want to break?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I would appreciate a short break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But I could start straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm trying to make life easier for you and for everyone actually. If you think a short break will help you organise yourself better, then I'll give you a short break.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So how much time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: About 20 minutes is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll have the break now. [Trial Chamber and legal officer confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Yes, we start at 12.00 actually. We start at 12.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Brdjanin is back in the courtroom. Madam Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may start. Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Chana:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you're an economist by profession, and you have told Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this Court you served in the in the security forces for 13 years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would make you, Mr. Savic, an extremely educated man, and you would be aware of all the political developments in the area at the time, in late 1991 to 1992. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would as a consequence of that also be privy to a great deal of information, would you not, by virtue of your position as chief of security?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible or is it true?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the type of information that reached me because in terms of hierarchy, I am the first at the municipal level. But in the state, I am at the fourth or the fifth level. First there is the minister, his assistants or deputies, then chiefs of CSBs, and then chiefs of public security stations, and then my assistant. So regarding the Municipality of Prnjavor, I had quite a lot of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You were the chief of the municipality, and I'll come to the hierarchy in a minute. But you were sent confidential reports, were you not? You sent reports yourself? Is it true?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would have to send reports, would you not, to your superior, Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in contact with the public at large?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of your duties, you would go around and talk to people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to various crime scenes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: There were no crime scenes in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no crime scenes in Prnjavor? What do you mean by that, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I mean murders and things like that. When you say "crime," what I understand is murder. Murder is crime, and that's what I mean when you say "crime." Crime scenes are murder scenes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not only talking about murder scenes, Mr. Savic. I'm talking about general crimes which were being committed in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we're talking about various aspects of criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wouldn't all criminal acts be within your purview as the chief of security, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is indisputable. However, there were no murders while I was the chief of police in Prnjavor. We did not have any murders, especially not amongst or between various ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people killed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the whole time --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Not in Prnjavor. From the moment I was appointed chief to the end of my career as chief of police, there were no murders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would murders according to you encompass killings? So there were no killings? I want to make quite sure that we are understanding each other.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was none of those either as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify again, what period are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: While I was the chief of police in Prnjavor and while I was in charge of Prijedor -- Prnjavor Municipality because I was responsible for the Municipality of Prnjavor. This is a municipality with some 50.000 inhabitants. And the town itself had a population of some seven and a half thousand people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the population of your municipality. I'm asking you about your statement that you just made to this Court that you were never informed of one murder or one killing in the municipality the entire time that you were the chief of security. Is that still a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Okay, killings, but what I had in mind were crimes between different ethnic groups. For example, if a Serb killed a Muslim or a Muslim killed a Croat, that is what I had in mind when you asked about murders and killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, it will help if you listen to my question. And I'm asking you just in very general terms that you would be aware of any killings or murders if they were to take place in your area of responsibility, which was the entire municipality, would you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your junior officers would bring you such reports, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were the man in charge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you brought it up, I will pursue that a little bit, but I'll come to it later on. How many reports of killings did you have at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't tell you. But I believe that there must be records on that. If there were any reports, they have to be recorded, and I believe that you can access those records. I really am not aware of any numbers. My subordinates would inform me about any such events, and this would be recorded in official records. I would also like to mention that I received regular daily reports every morning, and that I would forward them to my superiors. And if there was another --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will come to that in a minute. If you can just answer my questions as we go along because I would like to ask you some general questions before we get into the specifics. We're back to the killings, Mr. Savic. You cannot give me even an rough estimate as to how many killings were reported to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: How many we forwarded or how many we received?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many you were aware of in your security station of reports coming in.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Whatever happened in my police station, I knew about it. And if there was a killing, I would receive a report and I would forward it. And I state that in full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Savic, I can take it you're not prepared to give me an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm going to object to that, Your Honour. He said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't give you an estimate, no. I can't give you an estimate. The only thing I can say about any murder or any other crime for that matter is that they were covered by regular reports. They -- these things were reported to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about these reports. You sent these reports -- you said you sent a daily report up to Mr. Zupljanin, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, every morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the format of this report? Was it in writing? Was it oral? Was it standard? Was it faxed? How did it happen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: It was both verbal and written, depending on the situation. Reports were sent via dispatches every morning. And if so requested by the chief of the CSB, we would expand and write information about certain incidents that had happened in the territory of Prnjavor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savic. Did you make these reports available to your Defence counsel, or do you have them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't have them, and I did not make them available to anybody. This is all available in the police station, in the archives there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't bring or look at them to refresh your memory seeing that you were coming to give evidence in this Court about these events?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you one thing: I don't have any reports on any killings because I'm almost a hundred per cent sure that there were no Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. murders while I was the chief of police in Prnjavor. As for the regular reports, they were forwarded. And if I were to bring them, I would have had to bring a huge pile of daily reports. You may find it strange. I can see that you're finding it very strange, but there were no murders while I was the chief of police there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was the population of Prnjavor? What was the population of Prnjavor at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time about 50.000 or so. 47.000 according to the statistics. However, there was a lot of people who arrived from Croatia, the Serbian population who arrived from Croatia, and that increased the number of people to some 50.000 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And given that the population of Prnjavor was precisely something round about 50.000, what was the average annual number of homicides in such a small town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there were no homicides at all in 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On an annual basis, for example if I were to ask about Banja Luka, where the population is four or five times as much, you would expect more homicides to take place there than in a small town like Prnjavor. So were there figures for annual, average annual number of homicides in Prnjavor? Not just in 1991. Before the war, how many homicides in a year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war, below one a year. So it was really not a common occurrence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go ahead now and jump to something different because I intervened precisely because in a small town like Prnjavor, you don't expect any homicides beyond maybe one a year maximum.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not even one a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the entire municipality now. Do you know a village called Lisnja?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do because that was a neighbouring village to my village, the village where I was born.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was a predominantly Muslim village, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, predominantly Muslim, and there were some Ukrainians as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your area of responsibility would have included Lisnja, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any killings in Lisnja?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. There was, but later, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is later? Can you tell us the month, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: When I say "later," that is once I stopped being the chief of police. After my term of office, after the 1st of April 1992. There was an armed conflict in Lisnja between the Serbian forces and others. And it was not a classical homicide or murder. Three or four people died in that conflict, but that was after my term of office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard about it, so you were aware that it had happened?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that. I heard of that subsequently. I was already in Banja Luka at that time when I heard about that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said that there was a military operation with others. Would you define what these "others" are? Do you know? Who were the others? You just said in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Organised Muslim forces that carried arms, that were reinforced, that had their bunkers there and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which was the army formation from the Serb side which was part of this combat operation? Which corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the military subordination and command. I don't know who the participants were. I know that there were Veljko Milankovic's paramilitaries involved, and that the police was also involved, but in the part that had to do with prevention and things like that. So I wouldn't know much about the incident in Lisnja. I just know what I heard. But I didn't participate in that. I was not even in the territory when this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you were in Prnjavor, which was the corps in command of that particular zone, the geographical zone of responsibility? Was it not the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: It was the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps under Commander Uzelac. I believe this was his name. General Uzelac, I believe he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, it was General Talic was it not who was in command of the 1st Krajina Corps. Now, you said this military operation had been conducted by the army, the Serb army, the police, and Veljko Milankovic paramilitary group. You just said that in your transcript if I can refer you back to it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I said Serb forces. I can't give you any detail on who exactly was there. I cannot say that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, that's fine. I'll take Serb forces. Serb forces in conjunction with the police and in conjunction with the paramilitary formation of Milankovic. It was a coordinated effort. Is that not correct? Now, can I move on to the various organs which were functions at the time in the ARK region. You obviously were aware of all these political organs, were you not? All the various organs in the ARK municipality? There was the municipal crisis staff, and there was a regional crisis staff? There was the army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you aware there was a municipal crisis staff? Which municipal crisis staff are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Prnjavor, the one he was working in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware there was a Prnjavor Municipal Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the crisis staff was established on the eve of the war. That is, the end of 1991, beginning of 1992. The crisis staff of Prnjavor Municipality started as the executive board. The executive body of the municipal assembly. Which existed according to the law and constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Those organs were legal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The regional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm more familiar with the autonomous region than the crisis staff. We always talked about the autonomous region. I'm not familiar with the crisis staff. I -- we referred to, when we spoke about those things, was the autonomous region. Now, what organs existed within the autonomous region I didn't know because I found it a bit odd, strange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hand him back to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's backtrack here a little bit, Mr. Savic. I was asking you earlier on that you were aware of information. Did you own a television?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a radio?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were listening to all the developments which were taking place in the Krajina region of which you were very much part of, being the chief of security in one of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have time to listen to the radio and watch TV. But yes, I did hear things that were happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told this Court earlier on in your examination-in-chief that you were -- had been listening to the media, the press, the newspapers, and the radio. I don't know the transcript number. But do you recall telling this Court earlier on that you were aware of these things from the press? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's a misstatement. I don't think I went into the media with him, and to the extent that it goes beyond the scope, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't recall it either. Perhaps, Madam Chana, you could refer us to which part of his -- to the precise part of his answer during the direct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I do have it somewhere, Your Honour, but I don't think I could find it straight away. But I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Because the witness has admitted to the fact that he would listen to the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would say -- Mr. Savic, it would indeed be your duty to keep yourself informed of all developments, would it not, in the region?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was my profession to be informed, so this is indisputable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it can be equally your duty to keep yourself abreast of all the political developments, would it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The part to which we referred earlier on was page 49, lines 21 to 23. "I don't know Brdjanin personally, although I am witnessing -- testifying here today. I know him from TV and from the media."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "But I believe he could not have had much of a say there." That's with regard to the Mice. That's the only part I find.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honour, but the point being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also page 39, he was asked now while you were in Banja Luka during April through the end of 1992, did you become aware of an entity known as the ARK crisis staff? And his answer was yes, yes, I know, I knew it existed. It was not a secret. It was published in the media. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did know about the regional ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I'm saying that we were more familiar with the autonomous region. And obviously the crisis staff would be its executive body within that autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, when did you first hear about Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date, but it was sometime in 1991 or 1992. But I can't really give you the exact date because I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also knew or know now as well that he was the president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I considered him to be the president of the autonomous region. I wasn't aware of the fact that he was the president of the crisis staff there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll -- there are many documents which I'm going to show you in a minute, Mr. Savic, which referred to the regional ARK Crisis Staff signed by Brdjanin which must have been sent to you. Would you like to tell us whether you ever saw any documents coming from the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I was waiting for something to appear on the screen. I apologise. Only in Official Gazettes that we followed, but I never saw a document signed by Mr. Brdjanin, and I say that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the Official Gazettes, of course, the ARK crisis -- the regional crisis staff is on more than one occasion mentioned. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I saw the Official Gazettes, yes. And then of course, I did see Radoslav Brdjanin's signature there beneath some conclusions or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So back to the organs -- the various organs and institutions in the territory of the Krajina at the time, now, did you know Mr. Nemanja Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did know him, and I still do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: He is the president of the municipal assembly, or rather later on the president of the Prnjavor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So now we have two institutions here, Mr. Savic. There's a regional crisis staff, and then there's a municipal crisis staff. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, if there's a regional, then there must also be a municipal crisis staff because that's how things were organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same went for your security service. There was the Central Security Services in Banja Luka of which your superior was Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there was the municipal SJB of which you were the chief. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that mix, there was also an army. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you properly. Where was the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was the army, the main staff under General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And underneath him were various commanders with their cause?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's the usual way in which army's are organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there was the 1st Krajina Corps, which was operating in your zone of responsibility, which was Teslic, Prnjavor, Banja Luka. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Teslic, I'm not a soldier. But I think that Teslic was not in the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps. I think it was in the area of responsibility of the Doboj Tactical Group and the other municipalities you enumerated were in the zone of responsibility of the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was the 1st Krajina Corps who was in Prnjavor, according to you, and Banja Luka. Right? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, each organ that I've just mentioned, which is the regional crisis staff, the municipal crisis staff, the security services, both at the central level and at the municipal level, the army, the main staff, and all the corps, in this region comprising of many municipalities, but I only am talking to you about the ones that you are familiar with. Given all these institutions, would you not agree with me then there would be necessary to have a great deal of coordination amongst all these different institutions and organs?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I'm going to object. I'm going to ask her to specify the time period because he was in several different municipalities with different tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. I think you have to pigeon-hole this in particular time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are talking about the time Mr. Savic was the chief of security which would be in Prijedor [sic] in late 1991 -- to the end of 1992. Okay, he was there until April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because he was moving from one place to the other during that long period. Were you talking of the whole year?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, April apparently -- I mean, that's the time he left Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He left Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Let me take it up to April first, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to object to the question because the ARK Crisis Staff was not in existence until 5 May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The ARK Crisis Staff was not in existence in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Right. So we will take it till after April then. My question is really a general one in the sense of all these --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the crisis staff was formed, whether you were in Banja Luka or whether you were in Prnjavor, just from your general information, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Savic, would you tell me or tell the Court who coordinated the activities of all these various institutions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who coordinated them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I am not surprised because we've had something -- I don't know how many witnesses we've had in this case, but no one -- I don't think there is anyone who was indeed in a position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question had been -- it actually changed. Would he not agree with me that it would be necessary to have coordination? I think that was really the question as opposed to who coordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Especially in a time of crisis.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had there been coordination, this would not have happened. I really don't know who coordinated the overall situation. I was strictly oriented towards professionalism, and I knew that things were bad, and I also knew that I would be held responsible if I acted outside the confines of the law. I didn't get involved in politics. I was not a member of any party. There were extremists on all three sides, and I knew that one had to be very careful in order to survive. So I was oriented only towards my job. And I really didn't know who was coordinating. I think that had coordination been better, some things might not have happened, and maybe we would not be here today. But I really don't know who the coordinator was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the question really was, once again, and I only ask it this one last time, it would be necessary, and you answered that it would have been necessary, to have the coordination amongst all these various institutions and organs, and as His Honour pointed out, especially in a time of crisis.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it would have been necessary. But I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, can I now ask you that were you aware of the ethnic cleansing which was taking place in -- let's take first the Prnjavor Municipality, of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Could we have a time frame, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Because if we're talking of Prnjavor, he was there until the 1st of April. So let's stick to that first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, let's start until April 1991 [sic]. Were you aware at that time that there was a policy which was going to be implemented to --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Up to April 1992, there was no ethnic cleansing in Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did it start?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: In my view, it started officially when the war started, and that is in 1992. Everybody knows this, and so do I. But this did not happen in Prnjavor before April. Or rather, I think it was May, June, July when the problem in Lisnja happened. But there wasn't any ethnic cleansing up to that time. There was tension, but there was not ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, page 67, last line, line 25, that's -- the Prosecution was supposed to have asked the question "let's start until April 1991." It should be April 1992, just for the record. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you just give me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, can I ask you -- I'm back to the institutions again. In your mind, which was the highest institution at the -- in this period of time, 1991, after the war began? Either from Prnjavor or Banja Luka? You were in Banja Luka after April. Which was the highest institution which was directing all the activities of government? What was the government?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: In my view, there was a vacuum at the time. I think it was the assembly, the government, the leadership of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was what it was called at the time. But I wasn't sufficiently familiar with all of that. I thought that it was the police and the army that had to keep the security situation up to a certain level. As regards the executive authorities, the municipality of the autonomous region -- the assembly of the autonomous region and it was then called the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I think that the assembly should be the highest legislative authority. But I'm really not sufficiently familiar with the situation. In my view, it was the Assembly of the Serbian Autonomous Region or Republic that was the highest legislative authority, in my view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and when this regional municipal assembly could not sit due to the war, who took its place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, that depended on the area, but I think it was the municipal assembly. In Prnjavor, it was the assembly and its executive board. And later on in 1992, the executive board was transformed into a crisis staff. The crisis staff was something that existed in the legal terminology of the former Yugoslavia. In war situations, the legislation provided for crisis staffs to be established. There was a crisis staff in 1986 in Prnjavor when there was a flood for defence against the flood. In my view, the highest authority was the crisis staff as it was called at the time. But as far as I can remember, Prnjavor Municipality always had an executive board and the town assembly, the municipal assembly. And these were the highest authorities at the time. There was a 60-member assembly which had its executive board, and at one point in time it was renamed the crisis staff. But all this was functioning. I am referring to the Prnjavor municipality, and I assume that in other municipalities the situation it was analogous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But quite right. So when the assembly couldn't sit, the crisis staff resumed all the functions of the municipal assembly, is that not correct? At the municipal level?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: If the crisis staff was analogous to the executive council, then of course, that's how it would be. That's provided for in the legislation. If the assembly cannot sit, then it's the executive board that is responsible for the functioning of certain institutions in the Municipality of Prnjavor. In my view, I'm not a lawyer, but I do know some things. The executive board was renamed the crisis staff because of the time in which it operated and the situation in which it operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if that was true for the municipal level, it was equally true the regional level, when the regional assembly could not sit, all the functions were taken over by the regional assembly. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm going to object. He say he doesn't know about the regional level. I'm going to object because it calls for him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he speculates or whether he knows or doesn't know. Answer the question, please. If you think your answer will be just mere speculation, tell me so, and you will not answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only draw conclusions, but I have to say that I don't know. I don't know about the regional crisis staff. And to this day, I don't know who was in the regional crisis staff. I assert that with if you mean responsibility. I might be able to talk about Prnjavor, but not the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not ever hear Mr. Brdjanin on the TV in the media talking? Did you ever hear him in the media?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I did hear Mr. Brdjanin. I know what municipality he's from. He was on television. But mostly, I heard him mostly as a minister in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. government of Republika Srpska in the post-war period. I think he was the minister of building construction or whatever it was called. But I think he was qualified to be the minister because that was his profession. But to tell you the truth, I didn't really pay that much attention to political events because at the very outset, I was opposed to many things that were happening in politics, and I felt I shouldn't have much to do with that because as you know, I was not a member of the SDS. I was in the opposition in a way. I was different from Mr. Brdjanin. And the prevailing situation. And I knew Brdjanin mostly from television and from his speeches in -- the speeches he made as a minister before the assembly. As for the prewar events, the wartime events, I didn't know much about that as far as he's concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard Mr. Brdjanin making speeches, what did you hear him say?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember now. There were so many speeches, so many statements were made by Alija, Karadzic, and others. And I really cannot remember those quotations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for exact quotations, Mr. Savic. If you could just assist the Court in telling them some aspects, what kind of things would he talk about? For example, would he ever talk anything about the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: What I remember is that he engaged in exclusively professional discussions about the problems of his ministry. Everything that people said during the war sounded the same to me. Alija said he would sacrifice peace for Bosnia. He said: "Go to Serbia. This is Bosnia." Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about Mr. Brdjanin's utterances; not Mr. Izetbegovic -- Alija's. What was he saying about the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember that. So many statements were made that you could compile a book. I'm not referring just to Mr. Brdjanin, but all the politicians at the time. They were trying to outdo each other in what they would say and the people simply grew accustomed to that and stopped paying attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Try to limit, Mr. Savic, your answers to yes, no, where possible, and please try not to repeat yourself. You've already told us this three times. I know that you have been asked the question more than once, but try to limit your answers to what is just essential. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness a document, P227, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document is before you, Mr. Savic? Can you see it's a decision on the formation --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a decision on the formation of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's page 2. I'm not sure -- page 2. The list.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Decision. That's not it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring you to where there are a list of names. It's a decision. Are you with me, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the formation of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And it's signed by the president of the executive council, Nikola Erceg.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Nikola Erceg, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this before?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's look at it together. Now, it gives us a list of who belonged to the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the top you have Mr. Brdjanin as the president. Then you have Stojan Zupljanin. Do you see that in number 10?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Mr. Zupljanin was a member of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I really wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will now show you Document 202. I think the Defence have already shown it to you, but I would like to have it placed on the ELMO again, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, by Defence counsel. Now, you've just found out that Mr. Zupljanin was a member of the ARK Regional Crisis Staff. Perhaps this document will be looked at with fresher eyes. If you look at the beginning of this particular document --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- It talks about a meeting held on the 6th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it talks about who was present at this meeting. And then it says: "The chiefs of various municipalities" and Prnjavor is there.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you attended this meeting, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Finished on the 1st of April, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can take you to the portion the Defence counsel took you to, number 23.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where it says that "in all our activities, we're obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region." Are you saying that while you were there in April, that was not the directive, but after you left that was the directive which was given?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. There was even a directive that was dispatched which was quite contrary to this, where the ministry orders all subordinate officers to act in accordance with the orders of the minister. There is a dispatch to this effect. And had I known I would be asked about this, I could have found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have the dispatch here, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I don't. I don't. But there was one. I'm sure there was. And this is contrary to what was in the dispatch. I think in my personal view the chief of the centre wanted to let us know that we had to be responsible in our actions. And even after this came out, we worked only under orders from the minister and the chief of the centre. And I know that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was never even mentioned. We worked according to the instructions, regulations, and internal documents of the Ministry of the Interior. Why this was there, I think it was simply to let policemen know they had to be disciplined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Savic, which came first? The dispatch or this document that you have in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The dispatch was in 1991. It arrived in mid-June 1991. And it said that the police had to operate exclusively according to instructions from the ministry and not individuals from municipal governments. That was the gist of the dispatch. So not the local presidents and so on. There were attempts made in my case, too, but Vasic was not able to impose on me his views. This was the dispatch of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in May 1992, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In May 1992, I was in Banja Luka, in Banja Luka, in the crime investigation police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this particular decision supersedes that directive of yours because that was in 1991, and these are new instructions. Is that not correct? This one is dated 20th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no, the police continued observing these instructions. This Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is not a new instruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, this instruction -- your instruction you just told His Honour is in 1991. Is that not correct? If you would just answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This instruction is on 20th May 1992. Is that not correct? So these would be --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Instructions is it not, because the crisis staff is now formed, is it not? At the time of your dispatch, the crisis staff was not formed, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were executive boards, executive committees. However, this instruction --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, the crisis staff assumed all responsibilities of any other body, is it not, after 5th of May -- after it was established?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here. However, in full responsibility, I claim, as a policeman, that the police continued acting according to the legal enactments that were in force in 1991 because it is simply impossible to replace internally enactments by something that comes from outside. The police continued observing the enactments which dated from 1986. So whatever it says here did not have any bearing on the work of the police. And I claim that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have covered this sufficiently now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think we ought to go to something different.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to refer the witness to his own statement that we were given yesterday by the Defence counsel. Could he look at his own statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a problem, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I was just -- we had a rule, Your Honour, that if things are given to you they should also be given to us. And I just noticed that a whole bunch of stuff was just given to you, but it may have nothing to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are the documents that the Prosecution indicates --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- because they didn't have time. Our secretary has only managed to compile them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my first statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the -- I can't tell you what paragraph it is, but it's towards the bottom of the page where it says: "This kind of action..." Can you find a sentence beginning: "This kind of action..."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Are you referring to the sentence beginning with: "This operation by the CSB Banja Luka was carried out" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'll just read it out. And it says, and you can follow it on your paper: "This kind of action was conducted by the SJB Banja Luka whenever the municipal war presidencies asked..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which municipal war presidency are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: The municipal war presidency is a general term. There were several terms. The crisis staff, presidency, executive board. So these terms just replaced one another. The municipal war presidency is what I was going to say. There were several terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other term for it is the municipal crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. If that's what you think, then be it. The war presidency were members of the executive board of the municipality, and this was the executive board appointed by the municipal assembly at one of its sessions. Those were the municipal officials, the chiefs of various departments and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did take orders from the crisis staff, did you not? I mean, it says so in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's only logical. President of municipality could ask me to do anything that was in keeping with the law. He could have asked me to do things that were not in keeping with the law, but I would have refused. Even if nobody had ordered me to do this, I would have done in Teslic what I did without the municipal leadership. This is my signature. I'm a professional. So I would have done this even if I hadn't been ordered to do that by municipal bodies. Even Mr. Brdjanin would not have been able to order me that because I would not have been -- I would not have wanted to go there. Crisis staff, war presidency, I was a policeman. And it made no difference to me. What made a difference was that I had to go and do my job. And I would have done it even without Brdjanin, without Zupljanin, without anybody. I would have dismantled these collection centres, I would have reinstated law and order. I would have brought the police to keep law and order --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, I think the Judge has pointed out to you. If you would just please try to answer the question, we can go quicker. I appreciate all this knowledge that you wish to bring forward, but nevertheless. So you did take orders from different institutions, and one of the orders you said was --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no. This operation by the CSB, not the police station, I did not receive instructions from anybody but Stojan Zupljanin who was my superior, my chief of CSB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would take orders from your superior, Mr. Zupljanin, would you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would. Yes. I never received instructions from anybody else. There may have been some requests in accordance with the law. And here I worked exclusively on the orders of Stojan Zupljanin. And I remember a situation when I came to his office and when he dictated to all of us and ordered us to go to Teslic and deal with the situation there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the crisis staff gave orders to the police, the CSB, which is the central, passed it down to the local SJBs, did it not? There were orders --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't say anything to that effect. I don't know anything about the relationship between politics and the CSB. I was not up to speed with that. I don't even know whether there are any documents on that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you P195, if I may. This is -- have you got the document? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I actually come to this document, there was one other question I would like to ask on the witness statement where he says --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you say, Mr. Savic, that this is your first witness statement. How many statements did you make?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: That was my first official statement. I have given a few, not paying too much attention to the terms I used. But in any case, this is a truthful statement. I am not a legal professional. And to my mind what matters is that the essence is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, the question is really quite a simple one. How many statements have you made altogether, official or unofficial?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: There were many unofficial statements. But this is the first official one signed by me on this case. I made some official notes as a policeman. I don't know whether you're counting that, too, or when I informed my superiors about the events. But in any case, the only statement that I ever gave on this case is this one here, my first official statement on this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it your first and only, or is it just your first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My first statement, excluding the official circular letters when I was reporting on the developments --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are a policeman. We're talking of a statement being a document containing questions and answers that you gave to the Defence which we had a copy of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is my first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there a second one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it was the first and only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first and only signed by me in a conversation with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was showing you, Mr. Savic, P195. It's signed by Mr. Zupljanin, the chief of the centre. And it's to all the chiefs, all the public security stations, et cetera. It's dated 25th May 1992. And in it, this is your chief saying, and I quote: "In keeping with the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina regarding the surrender of illegally owned weapons and ammunition..."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, ammunition, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The line being: "In keeping with the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, what was the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was in relation to a decision, was it not, from the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were then asked to do various things, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: 14 May 1992. I was not asked directly, because I was a policeman, a simple policeman at that time. But if you will, to my mind, this is -- does not represent anything bad. What they're asking is for us to take certain measures. I have not gone through the entire text, but they asked us to do the ordinary police job. This is all in keeping with the law. There's no problem here. I can't read all of this, but in any case, I believe that everything it says here is in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you haven't taken my advice, and you keep ignoring it. Just answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You keep telling us many other things that we are not interested, or at least I am not interested in hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because like this, you're going to be here the entire week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, did you actually put this -- this plan, the concrete plans for the seizure of illegally owned weapons, ammunitions, and explosive, this plan that you have been talking about and you have been ordered to do so by your boss, in accordance with the decisions of the autonomous region, did you put it into effect, these orders that you were given?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't because I never received these orders. I personally never received these orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the police who did receive them would have put them into effect. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honour. That calls for speculation on his part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, if I could -- he has been talking about the police and the orders. And I think it's not really speculation as to when such an order -- can I rephrase that question and ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When such an order would have come, had you received it, you would have followed it, would you not? You just said to the Court, there's nothing bad there's nothing wrong in it. And such an order you would have followed it. It's from your boss, Mr. Zupljanin isn't it? Had you been in receipt of it, would you have followed it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I would have implemented anything that was in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in accordance with the law," Mr. Savic, would you take every order and research the law and decide for yourself that it's in accordance with the law? What do you mean by that? How would you decide what's in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I was familiar with many things. If somebody says "seize illegal weapons," that is in accordance with the law. All of these items I am familiar with, and I know that they are in accordance with the law. Give me anything, and I will even quote the provision of the law that this is from. For example, an illegal possession of weapons is against a certain provision of the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document, P294, please. This is dated 31st July. It's again from the chief of the centre, your boss. And it's addressed to all SJB public security stations. And -- it says: "Recently through the mediation of the Red Cross..." Have you got that, starting that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: "Recently".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're referring to the beginning of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, beginning of the document where it says that the Muslims have begun to depart from the Autonomous Region of Krajina to Croatia, Slovenia, and other Western European countries. And since we have learned that these persons are removing large sums of foreign currency from the AR Krajina, with the aim of standardising procedures in the inspection of convoys, we hereby issue the following instruction. And the instruction is, and it starts off with: At the meeting of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on June 1992, a decision was made, Section 3 of which stipulates as follows: Individuals leaving the Autonomous Region of Krajina may not take with them a maximum of 300 deutschemarks or a corresponding amount of other currency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You said "may not." It says "may."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Maximum of. Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means they can only take 300 deutschemarks as they leave the territory. Now, Mr. Savic, you'll agree with me that this order is passed on by your boss, and this was a decision made -- have you seen this document before, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you still then hold your position that the crisis staff were not giving orders -- I'm sorry, if I can take that back. That the orders did pass down to Mr. Zupljanin who passed them down to you and which were, in fact, implemented? Since you haven't seen this document before, but now it's here, would you like to reconsider what you have told the Court earlier about the instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: I adhere to my former statement. If I had been the chief of the police, I would not have implemented this because this is not in keeping with the law. Now, what was going on, I don't know. In any case, I never had a similar document in my hands before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is given by the chief of the centre following a decision from the ARK Crisis Staff, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here. It's indisputable. That's what it says. And I don't know how they maintained coordination amongst themselves. Who ordered whom to do things? If I had been the chief of police in Prnjavor at the time, I would not have implemented this order, and that is precisely the reason for which I was replaced. Because this is an example of something that is against the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, if I could just interject here again, this is sent to all the SJBs, all the security centres, is it not? So every single security centre is supposed to conform to this decision by the autonomous region, the ARK Crisis Staff. And you said that you yourself would not have followed it. Are there any other decisions that you did not follow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is misleading now, Ms. Chana, because you have been referring this set of questions to the witness as if he was still responsible at the time of the SJB in Prnjavor, while we're talking of a time frame when he was just a mere simple policeman in Banja Luka, who had only one responsibility, to carry out the orders that his superior in Banja Luka would direct him to or would give him.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: And he said he was replaced because --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, I appreciate that. But I was basically drawing the witness's attention to this document purely on the aspect of the decision by the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you're going to ask him about other orders, he doesn't even know about the existence of this one. And I'm not surprised because he is not supposed to know. This wasn't directed to the individual members of each --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- SJB, municipal SJB. It was directed to whoever commanded those municipal SJBs.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think I've mixed up two subjects very fast. What I would like to ask the witness is

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever have an occasion to not follow an order of Mr. Zupljanin, when he was the chief in Prnjavor up to April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I supposed to answer this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I didn't understand the question. I thought this was another comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll phrase the question myself. Until you were commander of the Prnjavor police station, was there any instruction or order that you had received from Zupljanin, Stojan Zupljanin, that you decided not to obey, not to carry out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there weren't any. Well, let me be very short and up to the point. There weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I want to show you P272. I'm sorry, Your Honour, I seem to have misplaced one exhibit. Here it is. No, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is again another document --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, P272, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another decision similar to the last one. It is -- 1st July 1992. You were not the SJB at the time, but nevertheless -- you obviously would not have seen this document before either?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm reading it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's again a decision which has been disseminated by your boss Zupljanin, a decision made by the crisis -- the regional crisis staff in the ARK, the ARK Crisis Staff. So would you agree with me, Mr. Savic, that Mr. Zupljanin was, after looking at the couple of documents that I've shown you, was following the directions of the ARK, or at least giving the directions to his juniors on decisions reached by the ARK Crisis Staff? These are all documents signed by your boss.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO SAVIC
